decisionsTitle: The test gate in minutes: one migrated database per run, workers capped at the cores, four shards in CI
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-20**, from his phone, after a release waited on CI: «The tests take way too long, I need to be able to deploy faster on demand». Measured on the pull request of BR-V3.63 (run 39399923386): `yarn check` ran 32 minutes on its one four-core runner — the 16 000 unit and database tests nearly all of it — while the eight e2e shards were done by minute 18; a release therefore waited about 36 minutes on the pull request's run before `yarn ship` could start, and the same again whenever a tree changed. Amends §171 (the worker count) and §504 (the one run that tests a tree); the hook's command and BR-REQ-090-02 stand.

**Where the time went.** About 370 of the 1 100 test files create a database (`createTestDatabase`): each started a fresh PGlite and ran every migration — 177 of them — before its first test: start 2.2 s, migrate 1.1 s, measured on this machine. That is some twenty CPU-minutes of identical DDL per run, in every shard and on every developer's commit. And `vitest.config.mts` asked for twelve workers whatever the machine had (§171 measured that on the owner's 32 cores); on CI's four cores, and on a cloud session's four, twelve PGlite starts fought for the same cores and `beforeAll` hooks ran past their thirty seconds — files reported as hook timeouts with no failing test.

**Decision — one migrated database per run.** `tests/helpers/pglite-snapshot.ts`: vitest's `globalSetup` builds the migrated data directory once, before the workers start — a PGlite with every migration applied, dumped with `dumpDataDir` (uncompressed, about 45 MB) into `node_modules/.cache/pglite/`, named by the SHA-256 of the journal and every migration file — and `createTestDatabase()` starts each file's PGlite from that tarball (`loadDataDir`, about half a second) instead of running the migrations. A migration added or changed makes a new name, so no stale snapshot is ever loaded; a runner without the global setup builds the file itself, written under a temporary name and renamed, so two processes never read a half-written tarball. The migration tests under `tests/integration/db/` keep building their own PGlite from the SQL files: they prove the migrations, which a snapshot would assume. Nothing a test proves changes — the same migrations, applied by the same migrator, to the same PostgreSQL; only once.

**The workers.** `maxWorkers` is the machine's core count, twelve at most (`os.availableParallelism()`): §171's twelve on the owner's machine, four on CI and in a cloud session, where the hook timeouts stopped at once.

**CI — the same command, cut into runners.** `yarn check` becomes `yarn check:static` (docs, secrets, migrations, types, lint) followed by `yarn test`; the hook still runs `yarn check`. `.github/workflows/docs-check.yml` runs the static half in the job `checks`, with the build and the start, and `yarn test --shard=i/4` in four `unit` jobs — vitest's own slicing of the files, whose union is exactly the suite, nothing skipped — and reports their joint verdict as the one check `docs-check`, the name branch protection requires and `yarn ship`'s `HOUSE_CHECKS` wait on (the §504 e2e aggregator's pattern: `always()`, red when any need is red, green without running when `tested-tree` found the tree passed). The e2e suite goes to **twelve** shards instead of eight: the longest of the eight ran sixteen minutes on BR-V3.63's pull request and was its last job; twelve brings each to about ten, for four more runners of the twenty GitHub lets a repository run at once (1 + 1 + 4 + 12 = 18). The pull request's run is now bounded by the e2e shards, about twelve minutes, instead of thirty-six; `tested-tree` still skips the push to `qa`, the release PR and the push to `main`. BR-REQ-090-02's rule — CI and the hook name one command — holds: what is split is the runner, never the command, and AGENTS.md §6.3 and §21 say so.

**Not changed:** what the tests prove, their number, the e2e specs, the concurrency suite, the `tested-tree` record, `yarn ship`, the release workflow, the migration workflow.

**Refused.** Skipping tests for a release «on demand» (the gate is what makes a release from a phone safe; the time, not the tests, was the problem); `isolate: false` — measured on a quarter of the suite: the import time fell from 327 s to 99 s, and 193 tests in 41 files failed on state leaked from the file before (mocks, memoized settings, module-level clocks), the wall time barely moving; a file that fails far from its cause is not a faster suite —, and one PGlite shared by several files, for the same reason; the `threads` pool in place of `forks` (measured on the same quarter: 3 min 37 s against 3 min 40 s, noise, for a different process model under PGlite's WebAssembly); a Docker PostgreSQL in CI for the unit suite (PGlite needs no service and the snapshot removes its cost); caching the snapshot between CI runs (it builds in four seconds); more than four unit shards (each pays a minute of checkout and install, and four already leaves the e2e shards as the longest job); more than twelve e2e shards (GitHub runs twenty jobs at once, and a run that queues on itself gains nothing).
changelogLine: - **Releases wait half as long on CI** — the test suite starts every database from one migrated snapshot per run instead of running 177 migrations per file, its workers are capped at the machine's cores, CI runs `yarn test` in four shards beside the static checks, reported as the one check `docs-check`, and the e2e suite in twelve shards instead of eight; a pull request's run takes about twelve minutes instead of thirty-six. No test was dropped. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.github/workflows/docs-check.yml`, then both run `yarn check` and nothing else — the hook as one command, CI as its two halves `yarn check:static` (the job `checks`, with the build) and `yarn test --shard=i/4` (four `unit` jobs, the union of the shards exactly the suite), their joint verdict reported as the required check `docs-check`, red when any of them is red and green without running when `tested-tree` found the tree passed; `yarn test` starts every `createTestDatabase()` from one migrated PGlite snapshot per run, named by the hash of the migrations, so a changed migration is never served a stale database, and the migration tests under `tests/integration/db/` still apply the SQL themselves; `maxWorkers` is the machine's cores, twelve at most; the e2e suite runs on twelve shards, both projects, their union the whole suite (2026-10-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the test gate in minutes: one migrated database per run, four CI shards
